name: Question 7
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/a4a1d43bc68a44db24d22767630573ebd9aafb646196e212640c24f2650e7b17.png)

Consider the triangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1-u}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation is already in matrix form 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/0d736c2e3fa2c4ba1872b045b8bdcf4def98a24337683e368bec337b810b6acb.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our triangle:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(0,-1),(1,0),$ and $(-2,0).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14039710/assets/1aed421f9d6458fb8b72a44c83703b3f1c0475cee9ef9ec2f0a4cfcaad74d7fc.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=3>0,$ this transformation preserves orientation.

[xy]=[1−211]⋅[uv]+[0−1].

Which of the following gives the image of Δ in the xy-plane under the action of T?

EXPLANATION

An affine transformation T:R2→R2 is a function of the form x=Au+b, where x,u, and b are column vectors in R2, and A is a 2×2 matrix.

Notice that the given transformation is already in matrix form

[xy]=[1−211]⏟A⋅[uv]⏟u+[0−1]⏟b

The transformation T maps the boundary of Δ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of Δ, we find the images of each side.

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

  • The matrix U containing all vertices of our triangle: U=[010001]
  • The matrix B that has the same shape as U and with the vector b in each column: B=[000−1−1−1]

The image of u under T is given by Au+b. So, by applying T to U, we get

AU+B=[1−211][010001]+[000−1−1−1]=[01−2011]+[000−1−1−1]=[01−2−100].

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the xy-plane are (0,−1),(1,0), and (−2,0).
